newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt mostly higher in quiet Monday trade.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt mostly higher in quiet Monday trade.

text.p: Emerging markets debt turned mostly higher in a late rally Monday, with holidays in London and some Latin American countries limiting volume, traders and analysts said.
Brady spreads over Treasuries narrowed five to 10 basis points for most countries, analysts said.
"Volume's very thin," one trader said. "Institutions are, for the most part, out of the market, and Bradys are trading tick-for-tick with Treasuries."
Peru drew solid demand in an otherwise quiet market, with some issues rising more than a full point, traders said.
"We've seen some customer buying the last three or four days, and I think it's just carryover from that," said one.
Interest in the country revived as players noticed Peru prices had lagged the rest of the market.

"We have good demand from Lima and from U.S. accounts, mainly for Peru discounts and Peru pars," another trader said. "They were buying those bonds at 200 basis points differential from Peru FLRBs and PDIs. That spread is very good."
Late Monday, Peru PDIs were up two points at 62-7/8 bid and Peru FLRBs were up 1-5/8 at 57-5/8 bid.
Earlier, Peru posted Gross Domestic Product growth of 5.2 percent for the year ended March 1997, compared with a 0.9 percent contraction for the previous year.

Traders noted limited selling of Brazil paper Monday in the wake of Friday's announcement of the larger-than-expected April trade deficit and the decree of credit curbs designed to slow import spending. By late afternoon, however, higher prices prevailed.
Benchmark Brazil "C" bonds were unchanged 1/8 at 77-3/8 bid, while discount "Z" paper was up 3/8 at 81-1/2.
In other Latins, Argentina FRBs were up 1/4 at 92-7/8 bid, and Mexico pars were up 1/2 at 74-1/8 bid.
Eastern Europe Bradys were broadly mixed, with Bulgaria IABs up 5/8 at 64-1/8 bid and Russian U.S. dollar Vnesh loans up 3/4 at 83-3/8 bid. Russian Min Fins were mostly lower.
